      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya</link>
      <description><p>Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/23/russia-ukraine-war-zelenskyy-libya-benghazi-drone-attack-ship-merkury-un-nato-europe-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya</a> on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.</p><p>Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <description><p>Island’s labour minister, Tony Dyer, says agreement acknowledges links between Speightstown and UK city are rooted in slave trade</p><p>A town in Barbados known as “Little Bristol” has signed a “twinning’” agreement with the UK city, marking a new chapter in a centuries-long relationship rooted in the transatlantic slave trade.</p><p>Barbados says the new partnership between Speightstown and Bristol is part of its wider push for reparatory justice, built in small steps rather than around a multi-trillion-pound claim.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/23/barbados-minister-speightstown-bristol-deal-slave-trade-reparations">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Brian Morales García of Texas seeks damages after he was wrongly identified as undocumented in case White House wants dropped</p><p>The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</a> recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant.</p><p>Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/23/trump-administration-deported-citizen-mexico">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/23/russia-ukraine-war-zelenskyy-libya-benghazi-drone-attack-ship-merkury-un-nato-europe-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen sets out 22nd package of sanctions</p><p><strong>Turning to Ukraine, Nato’s Rutte stresses the need to secure the flow of “crucial supplies” or air defence weapons and ammunition to Ukraine.</strong></p><p><em><strong>“</strong>It helps Ukraine to defend itself today, but it also strengthens Ukraine’s hands in any future negotiations with Russia. … But support needs to be concrete. <strong>We have to show Putin that his attempts to weaken our support will fail.”</strong></em></p><p><em>“Our citizens need to know that the lights will stay on, that their homes will stay warm, that hospitals, transport and communications will keep working.”</em></p><p><em>“One day it can be in the form of an arson attack against a factory or drones disrupt disrupting an airport. The next, it is sabotaged railways or cargo vessels targeted at sea and cyber-attacks.”</em></p><p><em>“It’s all happening now, and it won’t go away anytime soon. … <strong>The conclusion of all of this is that we are all targeted,</strong> that we are all affected – when it comes to our pipelines, our cables, our energy grids and our economies – and they are all interconnected. … That means that we are all in this for the long term, and <strong>therefore we must step up to the plate, to ensure that, we stay ahead of danger.”</strong></em></p><p><em>“But if we are serious about keeping our alliance strong and secure, then <strong>all allies must pull their weight not only in 2035, but starting now.</strong> At least, everybody needs to have the credible path to get there.”</em></p><p><em>“These investments are also a boon to prosperity. There are dividends to be gained from investing more in defence. This is about real jobs for real people.”</em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/23/russia-ukraine-war-zelenskyy-libya-benghazi-drone-attack-ship-merkury-un-nato-europe-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Burnham says it would be ‘unthinkable’ to rejoin EU without referendum</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-deal-eu</link>
      <description><p>Andy Burnham also said former Tory prime ministers who have criticised the revival of the Brexit debate were ‘stuck in the past’</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-europe-eu-uk-summit-deal-commons-cbi-farage-badenoch-haigh-politics-latest-news-updates">UK politics live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Andy Burnham has said it would be “unthinkable” for the UK to rejoin the EU without holding another referendum, offering his strongest commitment yet to directly consulting the public if he concludes Britain should go back in.</p><p>The prime minister is planning to set out the long-term options for closer ties with the bloc next month, with concrete steps coming after the next general election, as he has pledged to stick to Labour’s manifesto red lines.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-deal-eu">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/leaked-data-shows-more-than-1000-russian-military-suicides-during-ukraine-war</link>
      <description><p>Exclusive: Figures from cache of 11m death certificates reveal suicides account for about a regiment of Russia’s war dead</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/russia-war-dead-hidden-toll-ukraine-conflict">Russia’s war dead: the hidden toll of the Ukraine conflict</a></p></li></ul><p>In late October 2024, Alexei Bolgov, a sergeant guarding a military headquarters in the occupied Donetsk region, told his wife, Natalya, over the phone: “It’s horrific, what’s going on here. I’ll tell you when I get back.”</p><p>He never made it home. Five weeks later, shortly after turning 29, Bolgov walked about 300 metres from his unit’s command post near the village of Stepove into woodland and shot himself, according to a written account by his commander seen by the Guardian.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/leaked-data-shows-more-than-1000-russian-military-suicides-during-ukraine-war">Continue reading...</a></description>

French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:51:42 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>Macron pledges €350m for aviation research, pushes industrial acceleration</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261123-macron-pledges-%E2%82%AC350m-for-aviation-research-pushes-industrial-acceleration-choose-france-investment</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research, and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its reindustrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a2ef3750-e74c-11f1-a595-b587b1fd65db</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:46:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg">© Manon Cruz/Pool via Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261123-major-cyberattack-hits-it-systems-at-guadeloupe-university-hospital</link><description>
A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postponing non-emergency procedures.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dee6caee-e728-11f1-80df-9f0d9c8f7db3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:45:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg">© Carla Bernhardt/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a15be40c-e589-11f1-9ce2-a7af964aafae</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:44:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nicolas Economou</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-former-pm-de-villepin-launches-20207-presidential-bid-with-warning-to-far-right</link><description>
Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf6f11fc-e589-11f1-b2ac-0d673b4c7b00</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:02:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg">AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard - Aurelien Morissard</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-france-must-change-or-risk-losing-overseas-territories-former-pm-tells-rfi-manuel-valls</link><description>
France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c2eb5f78-e343-11f1-ac1e-392da9561c55</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:31:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg">© AFP - DELPHINE MAYEUR </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-greens-candidate-gives-hard-left-melenchon-a-boost-in-presidential-race</link><description>
French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">40b0fb0e-e4dc-11f1-a123-31d05317ef57</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:04:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg">© REUTERS - Tom Nicholson </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-depardieu-and-houellebecq-accused-of-gang-rape-on-french-film-set</link><description>
Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec3acb0c-e4dd-11f1-9619-3935a39ed096</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:24:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-france-probes-suspected-leaks-from-interior-ministry-to-far-right-national-rally</link><description>
France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5be0a25a-e4b2-11f1-be46-714476ef8919</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:55:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French union leader warns strikes will continue without higher wages</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-union-leader-warns-strikes-will-continue-without-higher-wages-cgt-sophie-binet-interview</link><description>
French trade unions have promised to call more strikes and demonstrations, arguing that a government proposal to increase the minimum wage fails to address the social crisis that has spurred protests across the country. Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, says even after six weeks of action, workers and students are more determined than ever to keep up the fight.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37c8b342-e40f-11f1-a821-bd0c1d2fd9c6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:07:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© REUTERS - Sarah Meyssonnier </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261119-podcast-living-on-minimum-wage-smic-35-hour-working-week-france-second-biggest-tax-csg</link><description>
The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians.

France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory.

A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968.       <title>Nvidia shares surge more than 30% on Jensen Huang‘s return, adding $1tn to company value – business live</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/23/tech-sell-off-ai-stock-market-support-measures-deployed-south-korea-taiwan-china-ftse-nasdaq-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>Donald Trump hails Huang as a ‘great patriot and national treasure’ after his surprise reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/23/donald-trump-democrats-republicans-presidential-primary-midterms-house-latest-news-updates#top-of-blog">US reactions to Jensen Huang return – US politics live</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-chief-executive">Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO</a><br></p></li></ul><p><strong>Shares in UK housebuilder Crest Nicholson have slumped by a quarter, to a record low, after the company issued a profits warning this morning.</strong></p><p>Full year completions were 1,353, at the bottom end of the Group’s previous guidance range of 1,350 to 1,400 completions.</p><p>The warning has hammered Crest Nicholson shares, which have lost more than a quarter of their value this morning, currently trading down over 30%. The brutal sell-off is also weighing on the wider sector, dragging peers like Barratt Redrow, Persimmon, Vistry and Bellway into the red.</p><p>Today’s update suggests that weakness in the housing market is no longer confined to first-time buyers. Crest Nicholson is predominantly exposed to the mid-premium family housing market, and the sharp deterioration in sales rates indicates that more affluent upsizers are also becoming increasingly cautious amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/23/tech-sell-off-ai-stock-market-support-measures-deployed-south-korea-taiwan-china-ftse-nasdaq-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips</p><p>Invoking Greek mythology, the US senator John Kennedy has characterized former <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nvidia">Nvidia</a> chief executive officer <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jensen-huang">Jensen Huang</a>’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the <a href="https://x.com/atrupar/status/2124514031209980207?a=ArDF3m1PBQGZjNDPrME&amp;s=20">most expensive</a> sex since Helen of Troy”.</p><p>The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/jensen-huang-testify-congress-nvidia-affair-spy">put at risk</a> by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/jensen-huang-nvidia-john-kennedy">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack</p><p>Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/september11">9/11</a>.</p><p>Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-down-today-live-update-outlook-teams-365-when-fixed-latest-status-cause-news">global Microsoft outage</a>. She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/22/hacks-ai-internet-outages-airlines-banks-microsoft-apple">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Amid air chaos, travelers will have to navigate an outdated system (and complex company policies if it all goes wrong)</p><p>Millions of people are planning to fly in the US over the Thanksgiving holiday, just two weeks after the US Federal Aviation Administration’s 13 November <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/faa-ground-stop-flights-explained">ground stop</a> halted all flights nationwide for the first time since 9/11 (aside from a brief halt in 2023).</p><p>In the chaos that ensued, some travelers embarked on <a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/royalcaribbean/comments/1xvkopq/comment/19smxjywidlcw/?context=3">overnight drives</a> to catch cruise ships and <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/women-stranded-faa-ground-stop-buy-ford-bronco-27-hour-road-trip-rcna609629">bought new cars</a> to make business meetings. Many had to simply cancel their plans and incur the costs that came with it. More than 18,000 flights were cancelled at a potential cost to travelers of $1.9bn in lost time and related expenses, <a href="https://www.andersoneconomicgroup.com/analysis-nationwide-ground-stop-cost-travelers-nearly-2-billion/">Anderson Economic Group estimates</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/23/thanksgiving-air-travel-us-explainer">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>When partners consider finances, when is it ‘my’ money, and when it is ‘our’ money? Guardian readers shared their experiences </p><ul><li><a href="http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2014/aug/08/end-loveless-marriage-financially-dependent">Private lives: ‘I want to end my marriage but I’m financially dependent</a>’<br></li></ul><p>A survey of about 1,000 Americans found that one in 10 would describe their partner as a financial bully.       <description><p>A citizen referendum, only the second of its kind in Georgia history, seeks to block a zoning amendment</p><p>Ire Gene Grovner stood behind his house on a recent morning, between chicken pens on one side and rows of winter collard greens on the other, holding a knife and skinning a raccoon splayed across a wood post.</p><p>“The meat is good roasted,” Grovner said.       <title>Brentford v Everton: Premier League – live</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/23/brentford-v-everton-premier-league-live</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Minute-by-minute updates on the 8pm UK kick-off</p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton">Haaland must be worried’: Moyes on Barry</a> | <a href="mailto:Daniel.Harris@theguardian.com">Email Daniel</a></p></li></ul><p>Though the standard at the top of the Premier League reflects neither its spending or self-mythologising, the level below that is perhaps higher than in any league, ever. Every team is organised, physical and athletic, with technical players in pretty much every position and various able to settle a game. As such, only seven points separate Bournemouth, in fifth place, from Ipswich Town, in 16th, results dependent not just on which side is better but who plays whom when, with final positions a reflection of what happens to be happening when the music stops.</p><p>Tonight’s match is emblematic of this condition. Only one side in that top 16 – 15th placed Fulham – have scored fewer than Everton’s 12 goals in 10 games yet, somehow, David Moyes’ men are seventh in the table. Brentford, meanwhile, are two points behind in 10th and, outside of the top four, only sixth-placed Leeds have conceded fewer than their 11 goals.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/23/brentford-v-everton-premier-league-live">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/uk-confirmed-hosts-2035-womens-world-cup-fifa</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Country’s first World Cup since men’s 1966 edition in England</p></li><li><p>Bid lists 22 stadiums as potential venues</p></li></ul><p>The UK is to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup, Fifa has confirmed. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the first World Cup hosted in the country since the 1966 men’s tournament in England.</p><p>The UK bid was the only one under consideration for 2035. The 2031 tournament has been awarded, also uncontested, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/2031-womens-world-cup-projection-fifa-ussf">to the United States, Mexico, ⁠Costa Rica and Jamaica</a>. The decisions were formalised at a virtual meeting of Fifa’s national associations on Monday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/uk-confirmed-hosts-2035-womens-world-cup-fifa">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/gianni-infantino-world-cup-sell-off-plan-96-years-documents-payouts</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Management team were in line for huge payouts</p></li><li><p>Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan</p></li></ul><p>Gianni Infantino’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/01/fifa-scraps-plan-to-sell-off-stakes-in-world-cup-after-widespread-backlash">failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan</a> could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian.</p><p>Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/gianni-infantino-world-cup-sell-off-plan-96-years-documents-payouts">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Emery insists no change of plan for Aston Villa despite Galatasaray surface</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/unai-emery-no-change-of-plan-aston-villa-galatasaray-surface</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager</p></li><li><p>Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday</p></li></ul><p>Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions League game at ­Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”.</p><p>Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work. Galatasaray played Saturday’s victory over Samsunspor at Basaksehir Fatih Terim stadium, a significantly smaller ground named after the former Turkey manager, who played for and managed Galatasaray.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/unai-emery-no-change-of-plan-aston-villa-galatasaray-surface">Continue reading...</a></description>

up for our free newsletter here</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/19/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">United’s victory at Anfield last season</a> was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.</p><p>Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">lost only 4-0</a>. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/mauricio-pochettino-can-now-see-just-how-desperate-manchester-united-are">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds</p><p>It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat.</p><p>The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/bayern-munich-jamal-musiala-controversy-bundesliga">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas</link>
      <description><p>Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change</p><p>“If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, <em>this</em> was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ikiN2ah9DL4">Pelé against the Nazis</a>. Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears.</p><p>In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of <a href="https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37625798/sevilla-real-betis-laliga-best-rivalry-city-lives-sport">a city divided</a>, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled <em>the </em>game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/pio-esposito-charles-de-ketelaere-inter-hat-trick-atalanta-serie-a</link>
      <description><p>Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta</p><p>This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born.</p><p>We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/nations-league-italy-france-spain-czechia">upset win against France</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/pio-esposito-charles-de-ketelaere-inter-hat-trick-atalanta-serie-a">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>WSL talking points: captain Spence inspires Spurs’ shock win at City and Lionesses impress</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal</link>
      <description><p>We may have a proper title race on our hands as City and Chelsea drop points and LCL strengthen their grip on third place</p><p>Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">shock 3-1 victory</a> away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. She is covering every blade of grass and leads by example. For me, she’s one of the best midfielders in the league.” <strong>Tom Garry</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">Match report: Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season</p><p>A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player</p><p>Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.</p><p>He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah.       <title>Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/mark-robins-stoke-birmingham-championship-premier-league-promotion</link>
      <description><p>The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit</p><p>There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/championship-roundup-southampton-birmingham-middlesbrough-swansea">second in the Championship table</a> and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight.</p><p>Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/mark-robins-stoke-birmingham-championship-premier-league-promotion">Continue reading...</a></description>

Berlin, Paris, Madrid, Milan, Vienne... Depuis vendredi, partout en Europe, des centaines de milliers de jeunes manifestent autour de deux mots d'ordre : pour l'avenir de la jeunesse, contre la vie chère. Ils dénoncent notamment la hausse des budgets militaires qui, selon eux, se fait au détriment de l'éducation, du climat et des services publics. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ccad0ede-e75e-11f1-b110-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T141550Z-2110561036-RC2PROAWCX8I-RTRMADP-3-EUROPE-PROTEST-BRITAIN.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ccad0ede-e75e-11f1-b110-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T141550Z-2110561036-RC2PROAWCX8I-RTRMADP-3-EUROPE-PROTEST-BRITAIN.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">07050e4c-e75f-11f1-8423-c1525c8a1742</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:35:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ccad0ede-e75e-11f1-b110-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T141550Z-2110561036-RC2PROAWCX8I-RTRMADP-3-EUROPE-PROTEST-BRITAIN.jpg">© Isabel Infantes, Reuters</source><dc:creator>Barbara GABEL</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Sénégal : le pétrole tient-il ses promesses depuis le premier baril en 2024 ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-le-p%C3%A9trole-tient-il-ses-promesses-depuis-le-premier-baril-en-2024</link><description>
🇸🇳 Deux ans après le premier baril de pétrole de Sangomar, le Sénégal peine encore à transformer ses ressources énergétiques en bénéfices pour sa population. Entre cherté du gaz domestique et une année marquée par des coupures d'électricité pendant l'été, le ministre de l'Energie et du pétrole reste optimiste.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2c00f718-e76b-11f1-b0ce-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-SENEGAL-P%C3%A9trole-Gaz.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2c00f718-e76b-11f1-b0ce-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-SENEGAL-P%C3%A9trole-Gaz.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">441244a6-e76b-11f1-9742-a13307aa2f5b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:33:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Questions directes</category><title>Échec de la COP31 : et maintenant ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/questions-directes/20261123-%C3%A9chec-de-la-cop31-et-maintenant</link><description>
La COP31 s’est achevée sans accord sur la sortie des énergies fossiles ni avancée majeure sur le financement climatique. Un nouvel échec pour la diplomatie climatique, alors que le réchauffement s’accélère. Les COP peuvent-elles encore faire avancer la lutte contre le changement climatique ?
 
Laurence Tubiana, présidente de la Fondation européenne pour le climat et ancienne négociatrice de l’Accord de Paris, analyse les conséquences de ce sommet.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f81264ca-e763-11f1-8f8c-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Francais-2026-11-23T17-26-02-214Z.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f81264ca-e763-11f1-8f8c-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Francais-2026-11-23T17-26-02-214Z.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1efc3eda-e764-11f1-943e-37b3aed138d2</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:46:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Florent RODO</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Navires russes ciblés en Libye : l'Ukraine étend le domaine de la lutte</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/europe/20261123-navires-russes-cibl%C3%A9s-libye-face-moscou-ukraine-%C3%A9tend-domaine-lutte</link><description>
Le président Volodymyr Zelensky a revendiqué lundi l'attaque de deux navires russes au large de Benghazi dans l'est de la Libye. Une opération spectaculaire destinée à frapper la logistique russe et remettre le dossier ukrainien au cœur des préoccupations internationales.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/856ab7e2-e754-11f1-8168-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26327310217136.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/856ab7e2-e754-11f1-8168-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26327310217136.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6084d98a-e71d-11f1-81c4-930cc6c98582</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:23:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/856ab7e2-e754-11f1-8168-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26327310217136.jpg">© SBU / AP</source><dc:creator>Grégoire SAUVAGE</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Football : l'Afrique soutient la réélection de Gianni Infantino à la tête de la FIFA</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-footbal-l-afrique-soutient-la-r%C3%A9%C3%A9lection-de-gianni-infantino-%C3%A0-la-t%C3%AAte-de-la-fifa</link><description>
⚽ La CAF affiche son soutien à Gianni Infantino pour un nouveau mandat à la tête de la FIFA. L’annonce a été faite par Patrice Motsepe, président de l'instance du football africain, lors de sa 48e assemblée générale ordinaire, samedi à Abuja au Nigéria.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c7f51d20-e757-11f1-8c0c-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-Afrique-FIFA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c7f51d20-e757-11f1-8c0c-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Couv-Afrique-FIFA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">10565f16-e758-11f1-bac8-75c9eaf1ef66</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:19:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Élément Terre, la quotidienne</category><title>Après l'échec de la COP31, quel avenir pour la diplomatie climatique?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/%C3%A9l%C3%A9ment-terre-la-quotidienne/20261123-apr%C3%A8s-l-%C3%A9chec-de-la-cop31-quel-avenir-pour-la-diplomatie-climatique</link><description>
La COP31 s'est achevée sans accord final. Les pays producteurs de pétrole ont fait pression pour que la sortie des énergies fossiles ne soit pas mentionnée dans la déclaration. Plus d'une centaine de pays se sont en conséquence opposé à son adoption sans cette mention. Cette COP était la première depuis l'annonce par l'ONU du dépassement "inévitable" d'1,5°C de réchauffement climatique. "Le monde ne peut pas se permettre que cela se reproduise", a jugé le chef de l'ONU Climat, Simon Stiell. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db1ec12e-e75e-11f1-aaee-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-371671ce.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db1ec12e-e75e-11f1-aaee-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-371671ce.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4ad0eb0e-e760-11f1-b781-ad27a2c984c6</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:06:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Audrey RACINE</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Belgique : le pays en grève  contre l’austérité  du gouvernement</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-belgique-le-pays-en-gr%C3%A8ve-contre-l-aust%C3%A9rit%C3%A9-du-gouvernement</link><description>
Alors que des dizaines de milliers de Belges protestaient contre l'austérité ce lundi 23 novembre, le roi Philippe a accordé un délai supplémentaire à Bart De Wever pour tenter de débloquer les négociations budgétaires. Le Premier ministre s'est donné jusqu'à la fin de l'année pour trouver un accord au sein de sa coalition, faute de quoi ce sera la fin de son gouvernement.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fcb36440-e75c-11f1-93ff-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/miniabelgique.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fcb36440-e75c-11f1-93ff-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/miniabelgique.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1a33ac50-e75d-11f1-8c11-4579bb4eb38e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:03:23 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Jensen Huang de retour à la tête de Nvidia dans un volte-face inattendu</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-jensen-huang-de-retour-%C3%A0-la-t%C3%AAte-de-nvidia-dans-un-volte-face-inattendu</link><description>
Le conseil d'administration de Nvidia a annoncé lundi la réintégration immédiate de Jensen Huang comme patron du géant américain des puces électroniques, sur fond de pression de Donald Trump, malgré un scandale mêlant adultère, espionnage et contrebande.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/61284b48-e75d-11f1-9500-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Retour-Jensen-Huang-Nvidia-10.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/61284b48-e75d-11f1-9500-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Retour-Jensen-Huang-Nvidia-10.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7686db76-e75d-11f1-9402-4579bb4eb38e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:51:58 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><title>🔴 Nvidia : les démocrates assurent que l'administration Trump et Jensen Huang feront l'objet d'enquêtes approfondies</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9co-tech/20261123-jensen-huang-r%C3%A9tabli-son-poste-directeur-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral-nvidia</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">82639a26-e75b-11f1-8095-af1a9ba786dd</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:34:30 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Nvidia : Jensen Huang retrouve ses fonctions de directeur général</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-nvidia-jensen-huang-retrouve-ses-fonctions-de-directeur-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral</link><description>
Nvidia a annoncé ⁠lundi que Jensen Huang ​reprenait avec effet immédiat son poste de directeur général de l'entreprise, spécialisée dans les puces pour intelligence artificielle, 11 jours après sa démission suite à la révélation de relations extraconjugales, dont l'une avec ​une espionne chinoise présumée.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/30a513b0-e759-11f1-a326-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-160055-160631-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/30a513b0-e759-11f1-a326-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-160055-160631-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">35ccd378-e759-11f1-95f5-2f13556ef93e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:25:01 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Égypte : le désert de Fayoum, trésor astral méconnu</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-%C3%A9gypte-le-d%C3%A9sert-de-fayoum-tr%C3%A9sor-astral-m%C3%A9connu</link><description>
Situé à environ 100 km au sud-ouest du Caire, le désert de Fayoum offre un ciel nocturne d'une grande pureté, loin de la pollution lumineuse des grandes villes, ce qui en fait un spot privilégié pour l'observation des étoiles et l'astrophotographie.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/326fb008-e757-11f1-b105-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-153241-153451-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/326fb008-e757-11f1-b105-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-153241-153451-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">375df03e-e757-11f1-b15e-bd81501e2538</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:14:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Gisèle Pelicot "humiliée" par l'utilisation de photos d'elle dénudée pour la promotion d'un essai</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261123-gis%C3%A8le-pelicot-choqu%C3%A9e-par-l-utilisation-de-photos-d%C3%A9nud%C3%A9es-d-elle-pour-la-promotion-d-un-essai</link><description>
Gisèle Pelicot a dit lundi être "profondément choquée" par l'utilisation de photos dénudées d'elle réalisées par son ex-mari comme matériel de promotion pour un essai critique sur la notion d'emprise. Devenue une figure de la lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes, elle a affirmé qu'elle userait de "toutes les procédures nécessaires" à l'encontre de la maison d'édition Tinbad.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dc823ac4-e758-11f1-96c6-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8DK8WE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dc823ac4-e758-11f1-96c6-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8DK8WE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff79ca94-e756-11f1-97b7-573bac8d4702</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:00:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dc823ac4-e758-11f1-96c6-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8DK8WE.jpg">© Valery Hache, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Royaume-Uni : une salle de concert évacuée après la diffusion d'une "substance inconnue"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-royaume-uni-une-salle-de-concert-%C3%A9vacu%C3%A9e-apr%C3%A8s-la-diffusion-d-une-substance-inconnue</link><description>
La diffusion d'une "substance inconnue" à forcé l'évacuation de 12 000 spectateurs venus assister au concert de Don Toliver à la Co-op Live Arena à Manchester dimanche soir. Selon la police, il pourrait s'agir de gaz lacrymogène.
 
 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6fc2e52e-e74d-11f1-9e90-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Evacuation-stade-Manchester0.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6fc2e52e-e74d-11f1-9e90-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Evacuation-stade-Manchester0.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a3188ca8-e74d-11f1-ad86-55c63efc8a9e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:00:13 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Le rendez-vous Afrique</category><title>Plaidoyer pour une IA 100% africaine</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/le-rendez-vous-afrique/20261123-plaidoyer-pour-une-ia-100-africaine</link><description>
Comment faire en sorte que l'intelligence artificielle ressemble et corresponde aux Africains ? En y intégrant leurs habitudes et leurs contraintes ? Dans une tribune au Monde, l'analyste en cybersecurité Yasmine Abdillahi déplore que “l’Afrique représente près de 20% de la population mondiale mais moins de 1% des données d’entrainement de l’IA”. Elle est notre invitée.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a8c01ca4-e755-11f1-bfad-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-62b8217b.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a8c01ca4-e755-11f1-bfad-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-62b8217b.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19468a8a-e756-11f1-8eda-8b281653e579</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:53:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Julien FANCIULLI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Moyen-Orient</category><title>Guerre en Iran : Téhéran réclame 290 milliards de dollars de dédommagements à Washington</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/moyen-orient/20261123-t%C3%A9h%C3%A9ran-r%C3%A9clame-290-milliards-dollars-d%C3%A9dommagements-washington-guerre</link><description>
Des tribunaux iraniens exigent que les États-Unis versent 290 milliards de dollars de dédommagements pour la guerre en Iran et leurs actions passées, a déclaré lundi un responsable judiciaire, citant également plusieurs actions en justice intentées contre les pays du Golfe pour leur soutien à Washington. De son côté, l'administration Trump a émis de nouvelles sanctions contre l'Iran, selon un communiqué publié lundi.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa41c35a-e752-11f1-b79b-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8AF3GC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa41c35a-e752-11f1-b79b-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8AF3GC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">44821a44-e750-11f1-9990-b7c2cab330c8</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:53:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa41c35a-e752-11f1-b79b-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8AF3GC.jpg">© Atta Kenare, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Navires russes attaqués en Libye : "des cibles légitimes" justifie Zelensky</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-navires-russes-attaqu%C3%A9s-en-libye-des-cibles-l%C3%A9gitimes-justifie-zelensky</link><description>
L'Ukraine a revendiqué lundi des attaques contre deux navires russes menées la veille au large de la Libye, dans ce qui apparaît comme une nouvelle extension de la guerre entre Kiev et Moscou. Les précisions de Jean-Paul Palomeros, ancien commandant suprême allié de la Transformation de l'Otan.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6d3e83dc-e74b-11f1-8f97-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-151338-151828-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6d3e83dc-e74b-11f1-8f97-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-151338-151828-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">728b57ac-e74b-11f1-a2e8-af4f4ebc6c00</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:36:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>Exclusif – Imane Khelif à France 24 : "J'ai été victime de manœuvres et d'agendas politiques"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261123-exclusif-imane-khelif-boxe</link><description>
Sacrée championne olympique aux JO de Paris 2024, l'Algérienne Imane Khelif s'apprête, à 27 ans, à boxer désormais chez les professionnelles. Sur France 24, elle se confie en exclusivité sur cette décision mais aussi sur la campagne de diffamation sur son genre dont elle a été victime pendant les Jeux et sa reconstruction après cette épreuve.

Gisèle Pelicot a dit lundi être "profondément choquée" par l'utilisation de photos dénudées d'elle réalisées par son ex-mari comme matériel de promotion pour un essai critique sur la notion d'emprise. Devenue une figure de la lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes, elle a affirmé qu'elle userait de "toutes les procédures nécessaires" à l'encontre de la maison d'édition Tinbad.
